title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 7th District
area: Most of Boston and adjacent cities including Chelsea, Everett, Cambridge, Somerville, Milton and Randolph.

context.text: Incumbent Ayanna Pressley ran unopposed in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary. No Republican candidate filed for the seat. Pressley is unopposed on the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Ayanna Pressley
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in both the Democratic primary and the general election.

summary.text: Ayanna Pressley is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 7th District. She was the first Black woman elected to the Boston City Council and the first Black woman elected to the U.S. House from Massachusetts. She is unopposed in the November 3 general election.

background.text: Born in Cincinnati, Ohio, in 1974, and grew up in Chicago, Illinois; attended Boston University from 1992 to 1994.
Worked as a senior aide to Congressman Joseph P. Kennedy II and Senator John Kerry before entering elected office.
Served on the Boston City Council from 2010 to 2019, the first Black woman elected to that body.

priorities.text: Fight to abolish U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), citing family separations and deaths in detention.
Protect and expand reproductive freedom, including access to abortion and maternal health care.
Expand access to affordable housing and tenant protections, including an eviction-assistance hotline.

positions.summary: Introduced a resolution affirming reproductive freedom as a fundamental human right and supporting policies including universal healthcare, maternal healthcare, and protections against pregnancy-related criminalization.
positions.quote: As we mark America’s 250th anniversary, we must also acknowledge that the fundamental freedoms this nation was founded on are not enjoyed by all its people—especially the right to one’s own body and reproductive freedom

positions.summary: Called for ICE to be abolished, citing family separations and deaths in detention, and opposed $70 billion in new funding for the agency.
positions.quote: ICE cannot be reformed—it must be abolished.

positions.summary: Sponsored the Eviction Helpline Act, which would create a national hotline to help tenants get assistance and know their rights before an eviction is filed.
positions.quote: Housing is a human right. It is health. It is dignity. It is stability and community. Every single person needs access to a quality home they can actually afford.

positions.summary: Criticized the Trump administration's tariff policy as harmful to families and repeatedly pressed for exemptions for essential baby products.
positions.quote: Donald Trump’s reckless and chaotic tariff policy is continuing to wreak havoc on our economy, and families with young children are no exception.

positions.summary: Opposed Republican cuts to the Affordable Care Act and Medicaid and called for extending ACA tax credits, saying Republicans are rolling back health coverage gains.
positions.quote: Republicans are rolling back these gains every day by gutting essential programs like Medicaid and forcing families to choose between refilling medications and paying rent.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, including the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
